# ADR-003 — Frontend-only wizard state

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Applies to** US-01, with shared state boundaries for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md), assessment pp. 2 and 6–9, and project owner's frontend-only data boundary

## Context

Step 1 must restore a draft when navigating back and reconcile from a newly retrieved form. Later steps depend on the same vehicle and policyholder data, plan selection, and terms and simulated payment status. Strapi owns business content. It does not receive customer, vehicle, quote, plan selection, or payment data.

## Proposed decision

Use a small Angular Signals store with explicit commands, typed snapshots, and read-only projections. Scope it to the app's quoting flow so route components can be recreated. Pass the country's decoded Router value to state accessors and store separate country snapshots. Never read a previous country's data while a new country is loading. Store normalized typed drafts with original field kind and stable field identifier; keep touch/submit and focus state in the component. The reconciler atomically replaces the active snapshot after a valid refresh and the store supplies the later-step projection only for the active country.

Use a small versioned, tab-scoped `sessionStorage` envelope for fictitious wizard state. The signal store owns the current state; the adapter writes full snapshots and validates the restored shape and country. Treat browser storage as untrusted, revalidate fields against freshly retrieved content before advancing, and reject malformed or unknown-version stored data. A recoverable content error retains the draft but blocks progression. If storage is blocked or fails, continue using memory for the current page session and make reload recovery unavailable. Clear the country draft when the user starts a new quote. Do not put quote data in URLs, cookies, analytics, diagnostic logs, content requests, or server persistence. App-opened separate tabs should omit `opener` where relevant. A duplicated or opener-linked tab can inherit an initial copy and then diverge. The design promises no cross-tab or cross-device guarantees. [HTML Web Storage standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)

The US-01 step-2 handoff can be verified with a same-country route or narrow screen that allows going back. It owns no plan UI or plan business behavior. Future deep links to plans or summary check the matching country and current prerequisites, then navigate to the earliest incomplete step within that country. Client guards are wizard navigation controls. The data boundary is implemented by the public API shape and the absence of quote-write operations. [Angular Router guards](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/route-guards)

## Consequences for later stories

- **US-02** consumes a current, validated Step 1 snapshot and published active country plans. Store only one selected plan reference per quote along with the calculated price snapshot and its inputs or revision linkage as specified later. A change to inputs or available plans invalidates dependent selections or totals when the later rules require it. Recheck prerequisites before summary.
- **US-03** derives the review from current country fields and masks the identity document in presentation. Use stable field purpose metadata to locate the document independently of its label. Bind consent to the current terms revision and quote snapshot. Proposed duplicate protection is an atomic attempt transition in the same store, from eligible to processing before the asynchronous simulation starts. Only the matching attempt can settle, repeat clicks do not enqueue, success keeps one confirmation number for that completed quote, and a reported failure may retry. The US-03 spec and checkpoint will decide how reload handles a persisted processing attempt and completed receipt. No real gateway, card data or global idempotency service is implied.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Memory only | Lowest retention, with loss on reload and no reconciliation of previously saved data after refresh. |
| Browser persistent storage or IndexedDB | Longer recovery and broader synchronization options, with unnecessary fictitious customer-data retention and more cleanup or coordination. |
| Server quote collection or hosted state | Could support cross-device resume and global deduplication, contrary to the frontend-only customer and quote data boundary. |
| General-purpose state management library | Provides conventions for large applications. Three wizard steps can share a signal store without that dependency. |

Verify same-country Back and Forward, country-switch isolation, restoration plus reconciliation after reload, graceful storage failure, and exclusion of quote data from network requests. Exercise duplicate payment attempts and reload outcomes under US-03. US-01 traces to AC-US01-06, 08, 09, 13 and 14 and T-US01-07, 08, 09, 13 and 14.

[Angular Signals](https://angular.dev/guide/signals)
16:- US-02 can use a separate Plan collection filtered by requested country, published status, and active flag, with stable plan identifiers, ordered plans, stored price/currency, coverages, benefits, and a recommended flag. US-03 can use a separate country Terms document with published text and a revision identifier. Their precise shapes, prices, and publication/acceptance rules belong to their future specifications. Changes to plans or terms need only their own publication.
18:## Public read boundary
20:The browser uses a same-origin `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/form` routed to Strapi through the static app host. Keep Strapi's ordinary Content API authorization enabled and grant the Public role the single custom `api::quote-content.quote-content.readForm` action. Enable neither generated CRUD routes for these content types nor public draft, preview, plugin, search, media, or admin actions. The frontend sends no authorization token. The static host proxies the dedicated read path only and returns no substitute SPA HTML for unmatched API paths. Admin access is a separate local binding and uses Strapi admin authentication for editorial access. [Strapi routing](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/backend-customization/routes), [Users & Permissions](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/features/users-permissions)
22:The controller takes the canonical country path parameter and no caller-controlled filters, locale, population, or publication selectors. It explicitly queries published data, populates only the known components, validates the whole content projection, and maps an allowlisted DTO. # ADR-003 — Frontend-only wizard state

**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-01-architecture-approval.md))  
**Applies to** US-01, with shared state boundaries for US-02 and US-03  
**Basis** [US-01 Draft 3](../../spec/US-01.md), assessment pp. 2 and 6–9, and project owner's frontend-only data boundary

## Context

Step 1 must restore a draft when navigating back and reconcile from a newly retrieved form. Later steps depend on the same vehicle and policyholder data, plan selection, and terms and simulated payment status. Strapi owns business content. It does not receive customer, vehicle, quote, plan selection, or payment data.

## Proposed decision

Use a small Angular Signals store with explicit commands, typed snapshots, and read-only projections. Scope it to the app's quoting flow so route components can be recreated. Pass the country's decoded Router value to state accessors and store separate country snapshots. Never read a previous country's data while a new country is loading. Store normalized typed drafts with original field kind and stable field identifier; keep touch/submit and focus state in the component. The reconciler atomically replaces the active snapshot after a valid refresh and the store supplies the later-step projection only for the active country.

Use a small versioned, tab-scoped `sessionStorage` envelope for fictitious wizard state. The signal store owns the current state; the adapter writes full snapshots and validates the restored shape and country. Treat browser storage as untrusted, revalidate fields against freshly retrieved content before advancing, and reject malformed or unknown-version stored data. A recoverable content error retains the draft but blocks progression. If storage is blocked or fails, continue using memory for the current page session and make reload recovery unavailable. Clear the country draft when the user starts a new quote. Do not put quote data in URLs, cookies, analytics, diagnostic logs, content requests, or server persistence. App-opened separate tabs should omit `opener` where relevant. A duplicated or opener-linked tab can inherit an initial copy and then diverge. The design promises no cross-tab or cross-device guarantees. [HTML Web Storage standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webstorage.html)

The US-01 step-2 handoff can be verified with a same-country route or narrow screen that allows going back. It owns no plan UI or plan business behavior. Future deep links to plans or summary check the matching country and current prerequisites, then navigate to the earliest incomplete step within that country. Client guards are wizard navigation controls. The data boundary is implemented by the public API shape and the absence of quote-write operations. [Angular Router guards](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/route-guards)

## Consequences for later stories

- **US-02** consumes a current, validated Step 1 snapshot and published active country plans. Store only one selected plan reference per quote along with the calculated price snapshot and its inputs or revision linkage as specified later. A change to inputs or available plans invalidates dependent selections or totals when the later rules require it. Recheck prerequisites before summary.
- **US-03** derives the review from current country fields and masks the identity document in presentation. Use stable field purpose metadata to locate the document independently of its label. Bind consent to the current terms revision and quote snapshot. Proposed duplicate protection is an atomic attempt transition in the same store, from eligible to processing before the asynchronous simulation starts. Only the matching attempt can settle, repeat clicks do not enqueue, success keeps one confirmation number for that completed quote, and a reported failure may retry. The US-03 spec and checkpoint will decide how reload handles a persisted processing attempt and completed receipt. No real gateway, card data or global idempotency service is implied.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Memory only | Lowest retention, with loss on reload and no reconciliation of previously saved data after refresh. |
| Browser persistent storage or IndexedDB | Longer recovery and broader synchronization options, with unnecessary fictitious customer-data retention and more cleanup or coordination. |
| Server quote collection or hosted state | Could support cross-device resume and global deduplication, contrary to the frontend-only customer and quote data boundary. |
| General-purpose state management library | Provides conventions for large applications. Three wizard steps can share a signal store without that dependency. |

Verify same-country Back and Forward, country-switch isolation, restoration plus reconciliation after reload, graceful storage failure, and exclusion of quote data from network requests. Exercise duplicate payment attempts and reload outcomes under US-03. US-01 traces to AC-US01-06, 08, 09, 13 and 14 and T-US01-07, 08, 09, 13 and 14.

[Angular Signals](https://angular.dev/guide/signals)

# ADR-004 — Published plan catalog and quote selection

**Status** Proposed · Pending human approval  
**Applies to** US-02  
**Basis** [Approved US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), [approval record](../approvals/US-02-spec-approval.md), and assessment pp. 2–3 and 7

## Context

[ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) reserves the country-scoped plan read boundary, [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) establishes the shared runtime decoder pattern, and [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) assigns selection and price state to the browser. US-02 needs the plan-specific read contract and a rule for revalidating the selection at the same-country summary handoff.

## Proposed decision

### Strapi publication and public contract

Use a Strapi Plan collection with Draft & Publish. A plan document owns its country (`co` or `cl`), name, short description, base price, currency, order, active and recommended flags, and ordered coverage and benefit lists. Lists use repeatable components with one plain-text entry each, so the plan and its lists publish together. Use the stable Strapi `documentId` as the opaque public plan ID. Republish keeps the same plan identity and a newly created document receives a distinct one. [Strapi Document Service](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service)

Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/plans` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing canonical API country parser and reject caller-provided query parameters. Query the Document Service with `status: 'published'`, `country` and `active: true` filters, and populate only the two lists. Read up to one record beyond the limit so an over-limit catalog fails without publishing a partial list. Isolate draft edits, and pick up publishes, unpublishes and active-status changes on the next read. [Strapi publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status) · [Document Service pagination](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/sort-pagination)

Project an allowlisted `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, plans }` envelope. Each plan projects `id`, `name`, `shortDescription`, `basePrice: { amountMinor, currency }`, `coverages: string[]`, `benefits: string[]`, `order` and `recommended`. The controller verifies source country and active status before projection. Database row IDs, draft metadata and component records stay outside the contract. Sort plans by ascending nonnegative integer `order`, then by ordinal `id` on ties. Preserve the configured order within each list and project the configured recommendation flag independently of selection.

Extend `@quote/contract` with a pure plan catalog decoder for Strapi and Angular. Reject mismatched version or country, duplicate IDs, non-Boolean flags, unsafe IDs or numbers, incompatible currency, missing fields, and malformed list entries. Bound a country catalog to 40 eligible plans and each list to 20 entries. Require nonblank plain-text values with at most 240 code units. A list may be empty. Reject the entire eligible catalog on invalidity. Render projected copy as text.

| Outcome | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Valid catalog, including no published active plans | `200` with the envelope. `plans: []` represents the empty state. |
| Unexpected query input or unsupported country | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` or `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY`, respectively |
| Invalid or over-limit eligible catalog | `503 PLANS_UNAVAILABLE` |
| Strapi read failure | `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` |

Reuse `{ error: { code } }` and `Cache-Control: no-store` for handler outcomes. Add only `api::quote-content.quote-content.readPlans` to the Public allowlist alongside `readForm`. Extend the exact same-origin proxy allowlist to the plans read path. Keep generated Plan CRUD, previews, raw CMS data and write credentials out of public access. Add fictitious startup plans for both countries using an independent, retry-safe seed that preserves editor changes and deliberate unpublication on later starts.

### Money contract

The configured Strapi base price is the final price. Store the editor value as a nonnegative decimal in major units and validate currency by country (`co → COP` and `cl → CLP`). Normalize by decimal digits to a safe integer `amountMinor` up to 999,999,999,999, with up to two fractional digits for COP and whole units for CLP. Reject excess precision or invalid values before serving the catalog. Use `Intl.NumberFormat` for `es-CO` or `es-CL` with the matching currency and precision. Keep one typed money value for the list and the handoff. The browser's validated Details snapshot is a navigation prerequisite. The price calculation has no dependency on that snapshot. [ECMAScript internationalization](https://tc39.es/ecma402/#numberformat-objects)

### Selection and route handoff

Keep the US-01 country-parameter and form-reconciliation flow. Extend the existing quote feature to recognize `/:country/quote/summary` as the same-country handoff seam. The live US-01 validator checks the current form and draft before entering Plans or opening the seam. Invalid Details return to the same country's Details, and a form retrieval failure keeps the form recovery path available. Returning to Details preserves its draft. [Angular route state](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/read-route-state)

- Read Plans after successful Details validation on entry or re-entry, on reload, country change and explicit retry. Use the existing `HttpClient` and signal-store pattern. Clear ready status during a read, cancel superseded requests and check country and request generation before using a response. A failed or invalid response leaves the user on the recovery path with progression blocked.
- Keep at most one candidate per country, containing an explicitly chosen plan ID and the price and currency at choice. Replace it when another plan is chosen. Restore the candidate from bounded, versioned, country-scoped `sessionStorage` as untrusted input, with the existing memory fallback. Keep the US-01 draft compatible. Starting a new quote clears its candidate.
- A successful re-read retains the candidate only if the plan still exists in the eligible catalog at the same amount and currency. A removed, unpublished, inactive or repriced plan clears the candidate and requires an explicit choice. A valid Details edit can keep an unchanged selection because price is independent of Details. An invalid draft or a request in progress or failing blocks use of the candidate. A temporary failure can retain the candidate for revalidation on retry.
- Continue requires a current valid draft and a ready catalog with a validated candidate. Every attempt to enter Summary, including direct or history navigation, checks Details and requires a candidate. When both prerequisites exist, obtain one fresh catalog response and keep the handoff closed during that read. Recheck the active route, valid Details and unchanged candidate before exposing the selected plan and final price from the fresh result. Missing or invalidated selection goes to the same country's Plans. Plan-read failures use the Plans retry state. Reuse that attempt's fresh result or failure on this redirect, so it cannot trigger a retry loop. This is a frontend quote-flow boundary. No quote data travels with the GET.

## Alternatives and consequences

| Alternative | Trade-off |
| --- | --- |
| Generated Strapi reads or embed Plans in Form Configuration | Generated reads widen the public contract. Embedding binds two independent publication schedules. The dedicated action adds one bounded contract and permission while keeping editorial workflows independent. |
| Trust the cached list or persist a full plan as a quote lock | Both save a handoff read and can carry withdrawn plans or outdated prices into Summary. Rechecking adds one request per attempt and validates against the response observed at handoff. A later publication can still occur after that response. |
| Clear every choice on any Details or catalog change | Simpler invalidation would discard explicit choices after unrelated edits. Preserving the choice only for the same eligible plan and price keeps Back and reload useful. |

Verify published country filtering, deterministic ties, draft-edit isolation, anonymous action restrictions, no-store, both country money formats and the valid empty list under AC-US02-01–03, 05–06 and T-US02-01–03, 05–06. Cover stale and superseded requests, price changes or removal between list and handoff, unchanged choice restoration, and direct or history navigation under AC-US02-04 and 06 / T-US02-04 and 06.

# US-02 — Plan selection design

**Status** Proposed · Pending human approval  
**Basis** [Approved US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md), and the [shared design system](US-01-design-system.md)

## Compare and choose

Keep the product-only header, centered wizard track, and centered Plans lane. Mark Datos complete and Plan current. Use **Elige tu plan** as the step heading and **Planes disponibles** as the visible group legend. Cards follow the published order. Pair consecutive cards across the wide lane and stack them in one column below the wide breakpoint. Match reading and focus order at every width. Let names, prices and lists wrap and grow vertically.

| Review specimen | Annotations |
| --- | --- |
| [Desktop comparison, Colombia](wireframes/US-02-plans-comparison-desktop.svg) | Esencial is checked and Ruta is recommended. The card separates short description, coverages and benefits. |
| [Existing mobile concept, Chile](wireframes/03-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the stacked layout. Apply the same card hierarchy as the desktop comparison and the price and action order below. |
| [Existing empty desktop](wireframes/10-no-plans-desktop.svg) · [mobile](wireframes/10-no-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the empty panel and **Volver a datos** action. Substitute the active country's name in the message. |

Lead each card with the radio and plan name, followed by the price and the short description. Show the published entries under **Coberturas** and **Beneficios**, omitting a heading if its list is empty. Use one final price from Strapi. Show the explicit currency code and local separators with `es-CO` and two fractional digits or `es-CL` and zero fractional digits. Examples are **COP 129.900,50** and **CLP 24.900**. Example amounts and plan copy are fictitious. Display the actual published plan content as plain text. Payment cadence is outside the current price contract.

Use native radios with a common group name inside a fieldset. Give each radio an explicit label containing its visible plan name. Associate its price and any **Recomendado** text as a description. Keep long coverage and benefit lists as readable content in the card. The radio and label row provide a 44 px minimum target. Use the checked mark and selected border and tint for selection, and a separate text tag for a recommendation. The fieldset starts unchecked unless an earlier explicit choice is restored and revalidated. [GOV.UK radios](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)

## States and actions

| State | Presentation and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Ready, unselected | Keep **Continuar** visibly disabled and place **Selecciona un plan para continuar** next to it. Offer **Volver a datos**. |
| Ready, selected | Enable **Continuar** when the current eligible choice and Details are valid. Selecting a different radio replaces the choice in place. Render Back before Continue in the visual and keyboard sequence. Stack actions on compact screens and use a full-width primary action. |
| Loading or retrying | Keep the Plans shell with **Cargando los planes…** and the shared [loading treatment](wireframes/07-loading-desktop.svg). Withhold cards and progression. Any placeholders are decorative and static with reduced motion. Keep Back available. |
| Revalidating before handoff | Keep Plan as the current step until the read succeeds. Show **Verificando tu plan…** in the same status area, with plan choices and further Continue activation unavailable. Back returns to Details and supersedes the read. |
| Empty | Show **No hay planes disponibles** and **Por ahora no hay planes para [país].** Offer Back. |
| Unavailable | Adapt the [shared recovery treatment](wireframes/08-unavailable-desktop.svg) with **Planes no disponibles**, **No pudimos cargar los planes. Intenta de nuevo.**, **Reintentar**, and Back. Keep progression blocked during retry and show only current results. |
| Reselection required | When a successful refresh removes or reprices the chosen plan, show the current choices unchecked and the message **Tu plan cambió o ya no está disponible. Selecciona un plan para continuar.** If no plans remain, use the empty state and explain the lost choice without instructing the user to choose. |

**Volver a datos** links to the same country's Details and leaves the draft intact. A valid unchanged selection can be restored after a fresh read. **Continuar** reaches the same-country Summary handoff only after successful revalidation. Use the existing step-navigation convention at the handoff. US-03 owns the summary content.

## Keyboard, focus and announcements

- Preserve native radio interaction. Tab and Shift+Tab enter and leave the group, arrows move and choose within it, and Space checks the focused choice. Keep focus on the radio after a choice. Use the shared visible focus ring and preserve the browser's checked mark in forced colors.
- Focus the step heading on route entry. If an activated control disappears during revalidation, move focus to the persistent step heading. When retry replaces its control with current results, return focus to the Plans heading. If a retry fails in place, retain focus on Retry. A user who moved focus to Back while waiting keeps it there.
- Use one polite status region for meaningful asynchronous changes, including loading, verification, successful retry and reselection. When moving focus to a recovery heading, let that focus movement communicate the recovery instead of announcing the same text twice. Native checked state conveys the radio change. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)

## Design review coverage

| Criteria | Review and later verification |
| --- | --- |
| AC-US02-01, AC-US02-02 | Confirm published order, copy placement and both price formats. Verify with long content and empty coverage or benefit lists. |

## Compare and choose

Keep the product-only header, centered wizard track, and centered Plans lane. Mark Datos complete and Plan current. Use **Elige tu plan** as the step heading and **Planes disponibles** as the visible group legend. Cards follow the published order. Pair consecutive cards across the wide lane and stack them in one column below the wide breakpoint. Match reading and focus order at every width. Let names, prices and lists wrap and grow vertically.

| Review specimen | Annotations |
| --- | --- |
| [Desktop comparison, Colombia](wireframes/US-02-plans-comparison-desktop.svg) | Esencial is checked and Ruta is recommended. The card separates short description, coverages and benefits. |

Lead each card with the radio and plan name, followed by the price and the short description. Show the published entries under **Coberturas** and **Beneficios**, omitting a heading if its list is empty. Use one final price from Strapi. Show the explicit currency code and local separators with `es-CO` and two fractional digits or `es-CL` and zero fractional digits. Examples are **COP 129.900,50** and **CLP 24.900**. Example amounts and plan copy are fictitious. Display the actual published plan content as plain text. Payment cadence is outside the current price contract.

Use native radios with a common group name inside a fieldset. Give each radio an explicit label containing its visible plan name. Associate its price and any **Recomendado** text as a description. Keep long coverage and benefit lists as readable content in the card. The radio and label row provide a 44 px minimum target. Use the checked mark and selected border and tint for selection, and a separate text tag for a recommendation. | State | Presentation and next action |

| Ready, unselected | Keep **Continuar** visibly disabled and place **Selecciona un plan para continuar** next to it. Offer **Volver a datos**. |

| Loading or retrying | Keep the Plans shell with **Cargando los planes…** and the shared [loading treatment](wireframes/07-loading-desktop.svg). Withhold cards and progression. Any placeholders are decorative and static with reduced motion. Keep Back available. |

name: git-workflow-and-versioning
description: Structures git workflow practices. Use when making any code change. Use when committing, branching, resolving conflicts, splitting uncommitted work in a messy working tree into clean atomic commits, opening or reviewing a pull request (PR), pushing to a remote, or when you need to organize work across multiple parallel streams. Use when cutting a release, choosing a semantic version bump, tagging, or writing a changelog. Use when asked to write a commit message or a changelog entry for a change, or to split a change into commits, even when the diff is pasted inline and the message seems easy to write from it.

# Git Workflow and Versioning

## Overview

Git is your safety net. Treat commits as save points, branches as sandboxes, and history as documentation. With AI agents generating code at high speed, disciplined version control is the mechanism that keeps changes manageable, reviewable, and reversible.

## When to Use

Always. Every code change flows through git.

## Core Principles

### Trunk-Based Development (Recommended)

Keep `main` always deployable. Work in short-lived feature branches that merge back within 1-3 days. Long-lived development branches are hidden costs — they diverge, create merge conflicts, and delay integration. DORA research consistently shows trunk-based development correlates with high-performing engineering teams.

```
main ──●──●──●──●──●──●──●──●──●──  (always deployable)
        ╲      ╱  ╲    ╱
         ●──●─╱    ●──╱    ← short-lived feature branches (1-3 days)
```

This is the recommended default. Teams using gitflow or long-lived branches can adapt the principles (atomic commits, small changes, descriptive messages) to their branching model — the commit discipline matters more than the specific branching strategy.

- **Dev branches are costs.** Every day a branch lives, it accumulates merge risk.
- **Release branches are acceptable.** When you need to stabilize a release while main moves forward.
- **Feature flags > long branches.** Prefer deploying incomplete work behind flags rather than keeping it on a branch for weeks.

### 1. Commit Early, Commit Often

Each successful increment gets its own commit. Don't accumulate large uncommitted changes.

```
Work pattern:
  Implement slice → Test → Verify → Commit → Next slice

Not this:
  Implement everything → Hope it works → Giant commit
```

Commits are save points. If the next change breaks something, you can revert to the last known-good state instantly.

### 2. Atomic Commits

Each commit does one logical thing:

```
# Good: Each commit is self-contained
git log --oneline
a1b2c3d Add task creation endpoint with validation
d4e5f6g Add task creation form component
h7i8j9k Connect form to API and add loading state
m1n2o3p Add task creation tests (unit + integration)

# Bad: Everything mixed together
git log --oneline
x1y2z3a Add task feature, fix sidebar, update deps, refactor utils
```

### 3. Descriptive Messages

Commit messages explain the *why*, not just the *what*:

```
# Good: Explains intent
feat: add email validation to registration endpoint

Prevents invalid email formats from reaching the database.
Uses Zod schema validation at the route handler level,
consistent with existing validation patterns in auth.ts.

# Bad: Describes what's obvious from the diff
update auth.ts
```

**Format:**
```
<type>: <short description>

<optional body explaining why, not what>
```

**Types:**
- `feat` — New feature
- `fix` — Bug fix
- `refactor` — Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
- `test` — Adding or updating tests
- `docs` — Documentation only
- `chore` — Tooling, dependencies, config

### 4. Keep Concerns Separate

Don't combine formatting changes with behavior changes. Don't combine refactors with features. Each type of change should be a separate commit — and ideally a separate PR:

```
# Good: Separate concerns
git commit -m "refactor: extract validation logic to shared utility"
git commit -m "feat: add phone number validation to registration"

# Bad: Mixed concerns
git commit -m "refactor validation and add phone number field"
```

**Separate refactoring from feature work.** A refactoring change and a feature change are two different changes — submit them separately. This makes each change easier to review, revert, and understand in history. Small cleanups (renaming a variable) can be included in a feature commit at reviewer discretion.

### 5. Size Your Changes

Target ~100 lines per commit/PR. Changes over ~1000 lines should be split. See the splitting strategies in `code-review-and-quality` for how to break down large changes.

```
~100 lines  → Easy to review, easy to revert
~300 lines  → Acceptable for a single logical change
~1000 lines → Split into smaller changes
```

## Branching Strategy

### Feature Branches

```
main (always deployable)
  │
  ├── feature/task-creation    ← One feature per branch
  ├── feature/user-settings    ← Parallel work
  └── fix/duplicate-tasks      ← Bug fixes
```

- **Release branches are acceptable.** When you need to stabilize a release while main moves forward.
- **Feature flags > long branches.** Prefer deploying incomplete work behind flags rather than keeping it on a branch for weeks.

### 1. Commit Early, Commit Often

Each successful increment gets its own commit. Don't accumulate large uncommitted changes.

```

```

Each commit does one logical thing:

```

update auth.ts
```

- `fix` — Bug fix

+# ADR-004 — Published plan catalog and quote selection
+
+**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-02-architecture-approval.md))  
+**Applies to** US-02  
+**Basis** [Approved US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), [approval record](../approvals/US-02-spec-approval.md), and assessment pp. 2–3 and 7
+
+## Context
+
+[ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) reserves the country-scoped plan read boundary, [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) establishes the shared runtime decoder pattern, and [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) assigns selection and price state to the browser. US-02 needs the plan-specific read contract and a rule for revalidating the selection at the same-country summary handoff.
+
+## Proposed decision
+
+### Strapi publication and public contract
+
+Use a Strapi Plan collection with Draft & Publish. A plan document owns its country (`co` or `cl`), name, short description, base price, currency, order, active and recommended flags, and ordered coverage and benefit lists. Lists use repeatable components with one plain-text entry each, so the plan and its lists publish together. Use the stable Strapi `documentId` as the opaque public plan ID. Republish keeps the same plan identity and a newly created document receives a distinct one. [Strapi Document Service](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service)
+
+Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/plans` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing canonical API country parser and reject caller-provided query parameters. Query the Document Service with `status: 'published'`, `country` and `active: true` filters, and populate only the two lists. Read up to one record beyond the limit so an over-limit catalog fails without publishing a partial list. Isolate draft edits, and pick up publishes, unpublishes and active-status changes on the next read. [Strapi publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status) · [Document Service pagination](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/sort-pagination)
+
+Project an allowlisted `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, plans }` envelope. Each plan projects `id`, `name`, `shortDescription`, `basePrice: { amountMinor, currency }`, `coverages: string[]`, `benefits: string[]`, `order` and `recommended`. The controller verifies source country and active status before projection. Database row IDs, draft metadata and component records stay outside the contract. Sort plans by ascending nonnegative integer `order`, then by ordinal `id` on ties. Preserve the configured order within each list and project the configured recommendation flag independently of selection.
+
+Extend `@quote/contract` with a pure plan catalog decoder for Strapi and Angular. Reject mismatched version or country, duplicate IDs, non-Boolean flags, unsafe IDs or numbers, incompatible currency, missing fields, and malformed list entries. Bound a country catalog to 40 eligible plans and each list to 20 entries. Require nonblank plain-text values with at most 240 code units. A list may be empty. Reject the entire eligible catalog on invalidity. Render projected copy as text.
+
+| Outcome | Response |
+| --- | --- |
+| Valid catalog, including no published active plans | `200` with the envelope. `plans: []` represents the empty state. |
+| Unexpected query input or unsupported country | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` or `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY`, respectively |
+| Invalid or over-limit eligible catalog | `503 PLANS_UNAVAILABLE` |
+| Strapi read failure | `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` |
+
+Reuse `{ error: { code } }` and `Cache-Control: no-store` for handler outcomes. Add only `api::quote-content.quote-content.readPlans` to the Public allowlist alongside `readForm`. Extend the exact same-origin proxy allowlist to the plans read path. Keep generated Plan CRUD, previews, raw CMS data and write credentials out of public access. Add fictitious startup plans for both countries using an independent, retry-safe seed that preserves editor changes and deliberate unpublication on later starts.
+
+### Money contract
+
+The configured Strapi base price is the final price. Store the editor value as a nonnegative decimal in major units and validate currency by country (`co → COP` and `cl → CLP`). Normalize by decimal digits to a safe integer `amountMinor` up to 999,999,999,999, with up to two fractional digits for COP and whole units for CLP. Reject excess precision or invalid values before serving the catalog. Use `Intl.NumberFormat` for `es-CO` or `es-CL` with the matching currency and precision. Keep one typed money value for the list and the handoff. The browser's validated Details snapshot is a navigation prerequisite. The price calculation has no dependency on that snapshot. [ECMAScript internationalization](https://tc39.es/ecma402/#numberformat-objects)
+
+### Selection and route handoff
+
+Keep the US-01 country-parameter and form-reconciliation flow. Extend the existing quote feature to recognize `/:country/quote/summary` as the same-country handoff seam. The live US-01 validator checks the current form and draft before entering Plans or opening the seam. Invalid Details return to the same country's Details, and a form retrieval failure keeps the form recovery path available. Returning to Details preserves its draft. [Angular route state](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/read-route-state)
+
+- Read Plans after successful Details validation on entry or re-entry, on reload, country change and explicit retry. Use the existing `HttpClient` and signal-store pattern. Clear ready status during a read, cancel superseded requests and check country and request generation before using a response. A failed or invalid response leaves the user on the recovery path with progression blocked.
+- Keep at most one candidate per country, containing an explicitly chosen plan ID and the price and currency at choice. Replace it when another plan is chosen. Restore the candidate from bounded, versioned, country-scoped `sessionStorage` as untrusted input, with the existing memory fallback. Keep the US-01 draft compatible. Starting a new quote clears its candidate.
+- A successful re-read retains the candidate only if the plan still exists in the eligible catalog at the same amount and currency. A removed, unpublished, inactive or repriced plan clears the candidate and requires an explicit choice. A valid Details edit can keep an unchanged selection because price is independent of Details. An invalid draft or a request in progress or failing blocks use of the candidate. A temporary failure can retain the candidate for revalidation on retry.
+- Continue requires a current valid draft and a ready catalog with a validated candidate. Every attempt to enter Summary, including direct or history navigation, checks Details and requires a candidate. When both prerequisites exist, obtain one fresh catalog response and keep the handoff closed during that read. Recheck the active route, valid Details and unchanged candidate before exposing the selected plan and final price from the fresh result. Missing or invalidated selection goes to the same country's Plans. Plan-read failures use the Plans retry state. Reuse that attempt's fresh result or failure on this redirect, so it cannot trigger a retry loop. This is a frontend quote-flow boundary. No quote data travels with the GET.
+
+## Alternatives and consequences
+
+| Alternative | Trade-off |
+| --- | --- |
+| Generated Strapi reads or embed Plans in Form Configuration | Generated reads widen the public contract. Embedding binds two independent publication schedules. The dedicated action adds one bounded contract and permission while keeping editorial workflows independent. |
+| Trust the cached list or persist a full plan as a quote lock | Both save a handoff read and can carry withdrawn plans or outdated prices into Summary. Rechecking adds one request per attempt and validates against the response observed at handoff. A later publication can still occur after that response. |
+| Clear every choice on any Details or catalog change | Simpler invalidation would discard explicit choices after unrelated edits. Preserving the choice only for the same eligible plan and price keeps Back and reload useful. |
+
+Verify published country filtering, deterministic ties, draft-edit isolation, anonymous action restrictions, no-store, both country money formats and the valid empty list under AC-US02-01–03, 05–06 and T-US02-01–03, 05–06. Cover stale and superseded requests, price changes or removal between list and handoff, unchanged choice restoration, and direct or history navigation under AC-US02-04 and 06 / T-US02-04 and 06.

+# US-02 — Plan selection design
+
+**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-02-design-approval.md))  
+**Basis** [Approved US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md), and the [shared design system](US-01-design-system.md)
+
+## Compare and choose
+
+Keep the product-only header, centered wizard track, and centered Plans lane. Mark Datos complete and Plan current. Use **Elige tu plan** as the step heading and **Planes disponibles** as the visible group legend. Cards follow the published order. Pair consecutive cards across the wide lane and stack them in one column below the wide breakpoint. Match reading and focus order at every width. Let names, prices and lists wrap and grow vertically.
+
+| Review specimen | Annotations |
+| --- | --- |
+| [Desktop comparison, Colombia](wireframes/US-02-plans-comparison-desktop.svg) | Esencial is checked and Ruta is recommended. The card separates short description, coverages and benefits. |
+| [Existing mobile concept, Chile](wireframes/03-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the stacked layout. Apply the same card hierarchy as the desktop comparison and the price and action order below. |
+| [Existing empty desktop](wireframes/10-no-plans-desktop.svg) · [mobile](wireframes/10-no-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the empty panel and **Volver a datos** action. Substitute the active country's name in the message. |
+
+Lead each card with the radio and plan name, followed by the price and the short description. Show the published entries under **Coberturas** and **Beneficios**, omitting a heading if its list is empty. Use one final price from Strapi. Show the explicit currency code and local separators with `es-CO` and two fractional digits or `es-CL` and zero fractional digits. Examples are **COP 129.900,50** and **CLP 24.900**. Example amounts and plan copy are fictitious. Display the actual published plan content as plain text. Payment cadence is outside the current price contract.
+
+Use native radios with a common group name inside a fieldset. Give each radio an explicit label containing its visible plan name. Associate its price and any **Recomendado** text as a description. Keep long coverage and benefit lists as readable content in the card. The radio and label row provide a 44 px minimum target. Use the checked mark and selected border and tint for selection, and a separate text tag for a recommendation. The fieldset starts unchecked unless an earlier explicit choice is restored and revalidated. [GOV.UK radios](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)
+
+## States and actions
+
+| State | Presentation and next action |
+| --- | --- |
+| Ready, unselected | Keep **Continuar** visibly disabled and place **Selecciona un plan para continuar** next to it. Offer **Volver a datos**. |
+| Ready, selected | Enable **Continuar** when the current eligible choice and Details are valid. Selecting a different radio replaces the choice in place. Render Back before Continue in the visual and keyboard sequence. Stack actions on compact screens and use a full-width primary action. |
+| Loading or retrying | Keep the Plans shell with **Cargando los planes…** and the shared [loading treatment](wireframes/07-loading-desktop.svg). Withhold cards and progression. Any placeholders are decorative and static with reduced motion. Keep Back available. |
+| Revalidating before handoff | Keep Plan as the current step until the read succeeds. Show **Verificando tu plan…** in the same status area, with plan choices and further Continue activation unavailable. Back returns to Details and supersedes the read. |
+| Empty | Show **No hay planes disponibles** and **Por ahora no hay planes para [país].** Offer Back. |
+| Unavailable | Adapt the [shared recovery treatment](wireframes/08-unavailable-desktop.svg) with **Planes no disponibles**, **No pudimos cargar los planes. Intenta de nuevo.**, **Reintentar**, and Back. Keep progression blocked during retry and show only current results. |
+| Reselection required | When a successful refresh removes or reprices the chosen plan, show the current choices unchecked and the message **Tu plan cambió o ya no está disponible. Selecciona un plan para continuar.** If no plans remain, use the empty state and explain the lost choice without instructing the user to choose. |
+
+**Volver a datos** links to the same country's Details and leaves the draft intact. A valid unchanged selection can be restored after a fresh read. **Continuar** reaches the same-country Summary handoff only after successful revalidation. Use the existing step-navigation convention at the handoff. US-03 owns the summary content.
+
+## Keyboard, focus and announcements
+
+- Preserve native radio interaction. Tab and Shift+Tab enter and leave the group, arrows move and choose within it, and Space checks the focused choice. Keep focus on the radio after a choice. Use the shared visible focus ring and preserve the browser's checked mark in forced colors.
+- Focus the step heading on route entry. If an activated control disappears during revalidation, move focus to the persistent step heading. When retry replaces its control with current results, return focus to the Plans heading. If a retry fails in place, retain focus on Retry. A user who moved focus to Back while waiting keeps it there.
+- Use one polite status region for meaningful asynchronous changes, including loading, verification, successful retry and reselection. When moving focus to a recovery heading, let that focus movement communicate the recovery instead of announcing the same text twice. Native checked state conveys the radio change. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)
+
+## Design review coverage
+
+| Criteria | Review and later verification |
+| --- | --- |
+| AC-US02-01, AC-US02-02 | Confirm published order, copy placement and both price formats. Verify with long content and empty coverage or benefit lists. |
+| AC-US02-03, AC-US02-04 | Confirm independent recommendation and selection, disabled unselected action, one checked radio, same-country Back and gated handoff. |
+| AC-US02-05, AC-US02-06 | Confirm the empty, loading, retry, revalidation and reselection treatments. Verify a repriced or withdrawn plan cannot reach the handoff. |
+| AC-US02-07 | Verify keyboard and accessible names and descriptions at desktop and mobile sizes, 320 CSS px reflow, 400% zoom, and focus through an unsuccessful and successful retry. |
+
+The project owner approved the design on 2026-11-22.

+# ADR-004 — Published plan catalog and quote selection
+
+**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-02-architecture-approval.md))  
+**Applies to** US-02  
+**Basis** [Approved US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), [approval record](../approvals/US-02-spec-approval.md), and assessment pp. 2–3 and 7
+
+## Context
+
+[ADR-001](ADR-001-multi-country-content.md) reserves the country-scoped plan read boundary, [ADR-002](ADR-002-dynamic-form-contract.md) establishes the shared runtime decoder pattern, and [ADR-003](ADR-003-frontend-quote-state.md) assigns selection and price state to the browser. US-02 needs the plan-specific read contract and a rule for revalidating the selection at the same-country summary handoff.
+
+## Proposed decision
+
+### Strapi publication and public contract
+
+Use a Strapi Plan collection with Draft & Publish. A plan document owns its country (`co` or `cl`), name, short description, base price, currency, order, active and recommended flags, and ordered coverage and benefit lists. Lists use repeatable components with one plain-text entry each, so the plan and its lists publish together. Use the stable Strapi `documentId` as the opaque public plan ID. Republish keeps the same plan identity and a newly created document receives a distinct one. [Strapi Document Service](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service)
+
+Add `GET /api/quote-content/v1/:country/plans` to the existing quote-content controller. Use the existing canonical API country parser and reject caller-provided query parameters. Query the Document Service with `status: 'published'`, `country` and `active: true` filters, and populate only the two lists. Read up to one record beyond the limit so an over-limit catalog fails without publishing a partial list. Isolate draft edits, and pick up publishes, unpublishes and active-status changes on the next read. [Strapi publication status](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/status) · [Document Service pagination](https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/document-service/sort-pagination)
+
+Project an allowlisted `{ schemaVersion: 1, country, plans }` envelope. Each plan projects `id`, `name`, `shortDescription`, `basePrice: { amountMinor, currency }`, `coverages: string[]`, `benefits: string[]`, `order` and `recommended`. The controller verifies source country and active status before projection. Database row IDs, draft metadata and component records stay outside the contract. Sort plans by ascending nonnegative integer `order`, then by ordinal `id` on ties. Preserve the configured order within each list and project the configured recommendation flag independently of selection.
+
+Extend `@quote/contract` with a pure plan catalog decoder for Strapi and Angular. Reject mismatched version or country, duplicate IDs, non-Boolean flags, unsafe IDs or numbers, incompatible currency, missing fields, and malformed list entries. Bound a country catalog to 40 eligible plans and each list to 20 entries. Require nonblank plain-text values with at most 240 code units. A list may be empty. Reject the entire eligible catalog on invalidity. Render projected copy as text.
+
+| Outcome | Response |
+| --- | --- |
+| Valid catalog, including no published active plans | `200` with the envelope. `plans: []` represents the empty state. |
+| Unexpected query input or unsupported country | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` or `404 UNSUPPORTED_COUNTRY`, respectively |
+| Invalid or over-limit eligible catalog | `503 PLANS_UNAVAILABLE` |
+| Strapi read failure | `503 CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE` |
+
+Reuse `{ error: { code } }` and `Cache-Control: no-store` for handler outcomes. Add only `api::quote-content.quote-content.readPlans` to the Public allowlist alongside `readForm`. Extend the exact same-origin proxy allowlist to the plans read path. Keep generated Plan CRUD, previews, raw CMS data and write credentials out of public access. Add fictitious startup plans for both countries using an independent, retry-safe seed that preserves editor changes and deliberate unpublication on later starts.
+
+### Money contract
+
+The configured Strapi base price is the final price. Store the editor value as a nonnegative decimal in major units and validate currency by country (`co → COP` and `cl → CLP`). Normalize by decimal digits to a safe integer `amountMinor` up to 999,999,999,999, with up to two fractional digits for COP and whole units for CLP. Reject excess precision or invalid values before serving the catalog. Use `Intl.NumberFormat` for `es-CO` or `es-CL` with the matching currency and precision. Keep one typed money value for the list and the handoff. The browser's validated Details snapshot is a navigation prerequisite. The price calculation has no dependency on that snapshot. [ECMAScript internationalization](https://tc39.es/ecma402/#numberformat-objects)
+
+### Selection and route handoff
+
+Keep the US-01 country-parameter and form-reconciliation flow. Extend the existing quote feature to recognize `/:country/quote/summary` as the same-country handoff seam. The live US-01 validator checks the current form and draft before entering Plans or opening the seam. Invalid Details return to the same country's Details, and a form retrieval failure keeps the form recovery path available. Returning to Details preserves its draft. [Angular route state](https://angular.dev/guide/routing/read-route-state)
+
+- Read Plans after successful Details validation on entry or re-entry, on reload, country change and explicit retry. Use the existing `HttpClient` and signal-store pattern. Clear ready status during a read, cancel superseded requests and check country and request generation before using a response. A failed or invalid response leaves the user on the recovery path with progression blocked.
+- Keep at most one candidate per country, containing an explicitly chosen plan ID and the price and currency at choice. Replace it when another plan is chosen. Restore the candidate from bounded, versioned, country-scoped `sessionStorage` as untrusted input, with the existing memory fallback. Keep the US-01 draft compatible. Starting a new quote clears its candidate.
+- A successful re-read retains the candidate only if the plan still exists in the eligible catalog at the same amount and currency. A removed, unpublished, inactive or repriced plan clears the candidate and requires an explicit choice. A valid Details edit can keep an unchanged selection because price is independent of Details. An invalid draft or a request in progress or failing blocks use of the candidate. A temporary failure can retain the candidate for revalidation on retry.
+- Continue requires a current valid draft and a ready catalog with a validated candidate. Every attempt to enter Summary, including direct or history navigation, checks Details and requires a candidate. When both prerequisites exist, obtain one fresh catalog response and keep the handoff closed during that read. Recheck the active route, valid Details and unchanged candidate before exposing the selected plan and final price from the fresh result. Missing or invalidated selection goes to the same country's Plans. Plan-read failures use the Plans retry state. Reuse that attempt's fresh result or failure on this redirect, so it cannot trigger a retry loop. This is a frontend quote-flow boundary. No quote data travels with the GET.
+
+## Alternatives and consequences
+
+| Alternative | Trade-off |
+| --- | --- |
+| Generated Strapi reads or embed Plans in Form Configuration | Generated reads widen the public contract. Embedding binds two independent publication schedules. The dedicated action adds one bounded contract and permission while keeping editorial workflows independent. |
+| Trust the cached list or persist a full plan as a quote lock | Both save a handoff read and can carry withdrawn plans or outdated prices into Summary. Rechecking adds one request per attempt and validates against the response observed at handoff. A later publication can still occur after that response. |
+| Clear every choice on any Details or catalog change | Simpler invalidation would discard explicit choices after unrelated edits. Preserving the choice only for the same eligible plan and price keeps Back and reload useful. |
+
+Verify published country filtering, deterministic ties, draft-edit isolation, anonymous action restrictions, no-store, both country money formats and the valid empty list under AC-US02-01–03, 05–06 and T-US02-01–03, 05–06. Cover stale and superseded requests, price changes or removal between list and handoff, unchanged choice restoration, and direct or history navigation under AC-US02-04 and 06 / T-US02-04 and 06.

+# US-02 — Plan selection design
+
+**Status** Human approved on 2026-11-22 ([approval record](../approvals/US-02-design-approval.md))  
+**Basis** [Approved US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md), and the [shared design system](US-01-design-system.md)
+
+## Compare and choose
+
+Keep the product-only header, centered wizard track, and centered Plans lane. Mark Datos complete and Plan current. Use **Elige tu plan** as the step heading and **Planes disponibles** as the visible group legend. Cards follow the published order. Pair consecutive cards across the wide lane and stack them in one column below the wide breakpoint. Match reading and focus order at every width. Let names, prices and lists wrap and grow vertically.
+
+| Review specimen | Annotations |
+| --- | --- |
+| [Desktop comparison, Colombia](wireframes/US-02-plans-comparison-desktop.svg) | Esencial is checked and Ruta is recommended. The card separates short description, coverages and benefits. |
+| [Existing mobile concept, Chile](wireframes/03-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the stacked layout. Apply the same card hierarchy as the desktop comparison and the price and action order below. |
+| [Existing empty desktop](wireframes/10-no-plans-desktop.svg) · [mobile](wireframes/10-no-plans-mobile.svg) | Reuse the empty panel and **Volver a datos** action. Substitute the active country's name in the message. |
+
+Lead each card with the radio and plan name, followed by the price and the short description. Show the published entries under **Coberturas** and **Beneficios**, omitting a heading if its list is empty. Use one final price from Strapi. Show the explicit currency code and local separators with `es-CO` and two fractional digits or `es-CL` and zero fractional digits. Examples are **COP 129.900,50** and **CLP 24.900**. Example amounts and plan copy are fictitious. Display the actual published plan content as plain text. Payment cadence is outside the current price contract.
+
+Use native radios with a common group name inside a fieldset. Give each radio an explicit label containing its visible plan name. Associate its price and any **Recomendado** text as a description. Keep long coverage and benefit lists as readable content in the card. The radio and label row provide a 44 px minimum target. Use the checked mark and selected border and tint for selection, and a separate text tag for a recommendation. The fieldset starts unchecked unless an earlier explicit choice is restored and revalidated. [GOV.UK radios](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)
+
+## States and actions
+
+| State | Presentation and next action |
+| --- | --- |
+| Ready, unselected | Keep **Continuar** visibly disabled and place **Selecciona un plan para continuar** next to it. Offer **Volver a datos**. |
+| Ready, selected | Enable **Continuar** when the current eligible choice and Details are valid. Selecting a different radio replaces the choice in place. Render Back before Continue in the visual and keyboard sequence. Stack actions on compact screens and use a full-width primary action. |
+| Loading or retrying | Keep the Plans shell with **Cargando los planes…** and the shared [loading treatment](wireframes/07-loading-desktop.svg). Withhold cards and progression. Any placeholders are decorative and static with reduced motion. Keep Back available. |
+| Revalidating before handoff | Keep Plan as the current step until the read succeeds. Show **Verificando tu plan…** in the same status area, with plan choices and further Continue activation unavailable. Back returns to Details and supersedes the read. |
+| Empty | Show **No hay planes disponibles** and **Por ahora no hay planes para [país].** Offer Back. |
+| Unavailable | Adapt the [shared recovery treatment](wireframes/08-unavailable-desktop.svg) with **Planes no disponibles**, **No pudimos cargar los planes. Intenta de nuevo.**, **Reintentar**, and Back. Keep progression blocked during retry and show only current results. |
+| Reselection required | When a successful refresh removes or reprices the chosen plan, show the current choices unchecked and the message **Tu plan cambió o ya no está disponible. Selecciona un plan para continuar.** If no plans remain, use the empty state and explain the lost choice without instructing the user to choose. |
+
+**Volver a datos** links to the same country's Details and leaves the draft intact. A valid unchanged selection can be restored after a fresh read. **Continuar** reaches the same-country Summary handoff only after successful revalidation. Use the existing step-navigation convention at the handoff. US-03 owns the summary content.
+
+## Keyboard, focus and announcements
+
+- Preserve native radio interaction. Tab and Shift+Tab enter and leave the group, arrows move and choose within it, and Space checks the focused choice. Keep focus on the radio after a choice. Use the shared visible focus ring and preserve the browser's checked mark in forced colors.
+- Focus the step heading on route entry. If an activated control disappears during revalidation, move focus to the persistent step heading. When retry replaces its control with current results, return focus to the Plans heading. If a retry fails in place, retain focus on Retry. A user who moved focus to Back while waiting keeps it there.
+- Use one polite status region for meaningful asynchronous changes, including loading, verification, successful retry and reselection. When moving focus to a recovery heading, let that focus movement communicate the recovery instead of announcing the same text twice. Native checked state conveys the radio change. [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)
+
+## Design review coverage
+
+| Criteria | Review and later verification |
+| --- | --- |
+| AC-US02-01, AC-US02-02 | Confirm published order, copy placement and both price formats. Verify with long content and empty coverage or benefit lists. |
+| AC-US02-03, AC-US02-04 | Confirm independent recommendation and selection, disabled unselected action, one checked radio, same-country Back and gated handoff. |
+| AC-US02-05, AC-US02-06 | Confirm the empty, loading, retry, revalidation and reselection treatments. Verify a repriced or withdrawn plan cannot reach the handoff. |
+| AC-US02-07 | Verify keyboard and accessible names and descriptions at desktop and mobile sizes, 320 CSS px reflow, 400% zoom, and focus through an unsuccessful and successful retry. |
+
+The project owner approved the design on 2026-11-22.

WORKDIR /app
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3 make g++ \

COPY frontend/public/icons/TABLER-LICENSE.txt backend/TABLER-LICENSE.txt

# US-02 — Plan card layout and selection revision

**Status** Proposed · Pending human approval  
**Basis** [Approved US-02 design](US-02-plan-selection.md), [US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), and [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md)

## Plan card layout

Set the centered Plans lane to a maximum of 58 rem. Base the card grid on the lane's available inline width after shell padding. Use 16 rem minimum tracks, 1.5 rem gaps, and one to three columns. Allow a single track to shrink below 16 rem when using a narrower lane.

| Available lane width | Capacity |
| --- | --- |
| Below 33.5 rem | One card per row |
| From 33.5 rem to below 51 rem | Two cards per row |
| 51 rem and above | Three cards per row |

Keep Esencial, Ruta and Integral together in one row at the widest size. Use the same rules for any published catalog size, collapse unused columns when the catalog is smaller, and place additional plans on the next row in published order. Match reading and keyboard order at every width. Reuse the existing card hierarchy and spacing, allow long plan names, prices, and list items to wrap, and let cards grow vertically. Test reflow without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS px and the equivalent 400% zoom. [CSS Grid track repetition](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#auto-repeat) · [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

## Whole-card selection

A click or tap anywhere within a ready card selects its plan. Keep one native radio per card in the existing fieldset, and associate the visible plan name with its radio through an explicit `label`. Stretch that label's transparent pointer target across the card. Keep the actual radio directly operable and the coverage and benefit lists in the reading order. Associate the formatted price and, when present, the **Recomendado** tag with the radio through `aria-describedby`. The radio is the sole selectable control, with the visible plan name as its accessible name.

Preserve native Tab, arrow key and Space behavior and the visible checked indicator. Show the shared focus outline for keyboard focus and keep it visible in forced colors. Selection updates the checked state and card emphasis in place without shifting the layout. Selecting a card leaves the user on Plans and makes **Continuar** available when the quote can progress. [HTML label element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#the-label-element) · [Radio group keyboard interaction](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/)

## Design review checks

# US-02 — Plan card layout and selection revision

**Status** Proposed · Pending human approval  
**Basis** [Approved US-02 design](US-02-plan-selection.md), [US-02 specification](../../spec/US-02.md), and [ADR-004](../adr/ADR-004-plan-catalog-and-selection.md)

## Plan card layout

Set the centered Plans lane to a maximum of 58 rem. Base the card grid on the lane's available inline width after shell padding. Use 16 rem minimum tracks, 1.5 rem gaps, and one to three columns. Allow a single track to shrink below 16 rem when using a narrower lane.

| Available lane width | Capacity |
| --- | --- |
| Below 33.5 rem | One card per row |
| From 33.5 rem to below 51 rem | Two cards per row |
| 51 rem and above | Three cards per row |

Keep Esencial, Ruta and Integral together in one row at the widest size. Use the same rules for any published catalog size, collapse unused columns when the catalog is smaller, and place additional plans on the next row in published order. Match reading and keyboard order at every width. Reuse the existing card hierarchy and spacing, allow long plan names, prices, and list items to wrap, and let cards grow vertically. Test reflow without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS px and the equivalent 400% zoom. [CSS Grid track repetition](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#auto-repeat) · [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

## Whole-card selection

A click or tap anywhere within a ready card selects its plan. Keep one native radio per card in the existing fieldset, and associate the visible plan name with its radio through an explicit `label`. Stretch that label's transparent pointer target across the card. Keep the actual radio directly operable and the coverage and benefit lists in the reading order. Associate the formatted price and, when present, the **Recomendado** tag with the radio through `aria-describedby`. The radio is the sole selectable control, with the visible plan name as its accessible name.

Preserve native Tab, arrow key and Space behavior and the visible checked indicator. Show the shared focus outline for keyboard focus and keep it visible in forced colors. Selection updates the checked state and card emphasis in place without shifting the layout. Selecting a card leaves the user on Plans and makes **Continuar** available when the quote can progress. [HTML label element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#the-label-element) · [Radio group keyboard interaction](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/)

- **AC-US02-03, AC-US02-04 and AC-US02-07.** Click or tap the radio, plan title, price, list text and card padding. Each hit selects that plan, replaces any prior choice and keeps recommendation distinct. Confirm the group exposes one radio per plan with name, description and checked state, and can be operated by keyboard.
